# 0109-xds-sds-combined-validation-context

Phase 66. Proves that under a downstream **`combined_validation_context` (CVC)**
the **SDS-delivered CA REPLACES the inline `default_validation_context.trusted_ca`
— it does not union with it.**

A disciplined clone of `0108-xds-sds-validation-context`: same observable shape,
same in-memory PKI machinery, same per-side SDS receivers. The one semantic delta
is the `DownstreamTlsContext`, plus a re-labelling of the two CAs.

## The delta vs 0108 (PLAN-66 D4)

| 0108 | 0109 | role |
|---|---|---|
| `CA_served` | **`CA_X`** — served over SDS | the anchor that MUST WIN |
| `CA_unserved` (never delivered) | **`CA_Y`** — inline `default_validation_context.trusted_ca` | a CONFIGURED competitor that MUST LOSE |
| `client_good` | **`client_X`** (signed by `CA_X`) | ACCEPTED |
| `client_bad` | **`client_Y`** (signed by `CA_Y`) | REJECTED |
| server leaf | unchanged (signed by `CA_X`) | — |

0108 proves the served CA is the anchor when **no** competitor is configured.
0109 makes `CA_Y` a real, parsed, configured inline default and proves the served
`CA_X` **beats** it. This **refutes Design C** (pool union): a union would trust
both CAs and **accept** `client_Y`. Only a REPLACE emits `bad=rejected`.

## Topology

```
                      SDS (SotW StreamSecrets, h2c)          in-memory,
  driver ──dial──▶ [ proxy: l_sds_cvc ] ◀── sds_cluster ──▶ driver-owned
   (2 arms)          tcp_proxy                                sdsserver.Server
                        │                                     (ONE per side)
                        ▼
                    c_backend (TCP echo)
```

One TLS-terminating `tcp_proxy` listener. Its `DownstreamTlsContext` carries:

- `require_client_certificate: true` — was **MANDATORY** under phase-66 scope
  (PLAN-66 D1): without it envoy-go **rejected** the downstream CVC at parse
  time (the E3 guard). Phase 67/ADR-0289 **lifts** E3 — the flag is now a
  **choice** for the CVC shape (verify-if-presented at false/absent; fixture
  `0110` covers it). This fixture retains `true` to keep its cross-CA
  substitution observable.
- a **STATIC** server cert (`tls_certificates`, `inline_string`, signed by
  `CA_X`), and
- a **`combined_validation_context`** nesting:
  - `default_validation_context.trusted_ca` = inline `CA_Y` PEM (the competitor),
    and
  - `validation_context_sds_secret_config` naming secret `validation_ca`, fetched
    over a SotW SDS gRPC stream against `sds_cluster`.

Only the validation context arrives via SDS, so boot's SDS pre-scan sees exactly
one secret — the CVC's **inner** SDS half, which PLAN-66 T4 taught the pre-scan to
count — and the deferred compose-two edge is never touched. Each side gets its
**own** SDS receiver (`reference_periodic_sink_differential_two_receivers`).

The served wire is **byte-identical to 0108's**: the management server cannot tell
a CVC client from a plain-SDS client (SPEC §8), so `test/helpers/sdsserver` is
**untouched**.

Reference: Envoy contrib-v1.37.2, `STRICT_DNS` via `host.docker.internal`,
listener port **10445**. Subject: envoy-go, `STATIC`, loopback.

## The PKI — in memory, per run; there is no `pki/` dir (PLAN-66 D2)

Six artifacts generated by `ensure()` with `crypto/x509` (ECDSA P-256, the `0018`
`pki/gen.go` crypto shape), **none of which touch disk**:

| artifact | issuer | role |
|---|---|---|
| `CA_X` | self | **the anchor that MUST win** — served over SDS as `trusted_ca` |
| server leaf | `CA_X` | `ServerAuth`, SAN `DNS:l_sds_cvc.fixture.test`; injected `inline_string` into both yamls |
| `client_X` | `CA_X` | `ClientAuth` — **must be ACCEPTED** |
| `CA_Y` | self | inline `default_validation_context.trusted_ca` — **the anchor that MUST lose** |
| `client_Y` | `CA_Y` | `ClientAuth` — **must be REJECTED** (proves REPLACE, not union) |

`CA_X` and `CA_Y` are both injected `inline_string:` (as PEM under a block
scalar via the driver's `indentPEM`) — `CA_X` out over SDS, `CA_Y` inline in the
bootstrap. Per-run freshness is safe: the observable is an accept/reject verdict.

> The two PEM substitution keys are documented in the YAML headers **without**
> their template-action braces. `text/template` expands actions inside YAML
> comments too, and a multi-line PEM expanded into a `#` comment splatters its
> continuation lines out of the comment.

## The two arms (the observable)

Both arms fold into ONE byte stream. Both sides must emit, byte-identically:

```
good=ok echo=phase66-cvc-probe
bad=rejected
```

1. **positive** — dial presenting `client_X` (chains to the SERVED `CA_X`):
   handshake succeeds, write `phase66-cvc-probe\n`, read the echo back through
   `tcp_proxy`. The backend IS exercised; `BackendCount()` returns 1
   (`reference_differential_backendcount_min_one`).
2. **negative** — dial presenting `client_Y` (chains to the INLINE `CA_Y`): the
   round trip MUST fail → `bad=rejected`. If it succeeds the driver records
   `bad=ACCEPTED` — the exact union signal this fixture exists to catch.

Each arm drives the **full round trip**, not just the handshake: under TLS 1.3 the
server's verdict on the client cert arrives *after* the client's `Handshake()` has
already returned. The dial is inlined in the driver because neither
`helpers.TLSServedLeaf` nor `helpers.TLSRoundTrip` can present a client cert.

## Served-this-arm precondition (SPEC §8 stale-server trap)

Before running the arms, the driver asserts that **this run's** per-side SDS
receiver recorded at least one `StreamSecrets` request (from the proxy's boot-time
initial fetch). A stale server that silently served a previous arm's config once
nearly produced a false divergence; per-side servers on separately-allocated ports
make that structurally impossible here, but the driver asserts it directly rather
than trust the structure. **0108 lacks this assert; 0109 adds it** (0108 itself
stays untouched).

## ⚠️ Why the driver carries a structural check

`CompareBytes` alone would make the proposition under test *"both sides agree"* —
which is **not** *"the served CA replaces the inline default"*. The breaks that
matter are **symmetric**: changing the served CA, or re-signing `client_Y` with
it, changes **both sides identically**, so the two streams still compare EQUAL and
a pure-`CompareBytes` fixture passes green
(`reference_vacuous_break_receiver_normalizes`).

This was confirmed empirically at Task 6, not assumed: with `structuralCheck`
disabled, the served-CA break **passes**. So `driveSide` asserts each side's OWN
bytes against the single correct stream; the runner turns a deviation into
`t.Fatalf("<side> drive: ...")`, naming the side and the violated arm. Both arms
are checked independently and all violations are reported together
(`reference_fatalf_makes_assertions_unreachable`).

`CompareBytes` is retained as the harness-standard cross-side leg and was proven
live by isolating it (asymmetric break with the structural check disabled → a
mismatch at byte offset 5).

## Why the failure text is normalized

The reference (BoringSSL) sends the TLS alert `unknown ca`; envoy-go (Go
`crypto/tls`) sends `bad certificate`. **A driver asserting the error string
cross-side fails 100% of the time** (inherits PLAN-65 C3). The negative arm
records only the stable token `rejected`.

## Coverage boundaries (named, unasserted)

- The **§3.9 empty-dynamic departure** is NOT on this fixture's cross-side path
  (one fixture dir = ONE runner branch,
  `reference_differential_fixture_dispatch_constraint`): the reference ACKs an
  empty dynamic context, falls back to the inline default CA, and SERVES;
  envoy-go boot-FAILS. That divergence is covered as a **subject-side unit test at
  T3**, not as a differential arm here.
- *(Retired at phase 67/ADR-0289.)* The **`require_client_certificate == false`
  / E3** boundary — under phase-66 scope envoy-go rejected a downstream CVC at
  false (PLAN-66 D1). Phase 67 lifts E3 across all three validation shapes
  (verify-if-presented); the flag is now a choice, and fixture `0110` covers
  the false arm. This fixture continues to always set it `true`, to preserve
  its cross-CA substitution observable.
- **No `ssl.*` stats** — envoy-go emits none, so a negative-arm `StatsAsserter` is
  infeasible (inherits PLAN-65 C3); a pre-existing framework gap.

## Running

Always use the FULL selector (`reference_differential_run_selector` — a bare
`-run '0109'` matches ZERO subtests and reports a vacuous green):

```bash
go test ./test/differential/ -count=1 -run 'TestDifferential/0109-xds-sds-combined-validation-context' -v
```
